interface.title: KinetiQC Research Explorer
interface.field: Neuroimaging: dynamic brain PET quantification and protocol robustness
interface.stage_of_work: Results exploration and interpretation of precomputed (cached) benchmark artifacts after the analysis pipeline has run
interface.what_it_is_for: Shows how far a dynamic brain PET acquisition can be shortened, subsampled, made noisier or moved before regional time-activity measures, connectivity matrices and radiomic features stop being reliable, and whether simple temporal recovery restores them.

data.note: The app has no upload and runs no computations. It reads cached tables: the real outputs/final-benchmark tables for 3 NRM2018 / OpenNeuro ds001705 subjects (369 subject-level rows, 11 stress scenarios, 0 audit failures), plus synthetic seed data for subjects 000101–000103 and sessions baseline/displaced on the TAC, Kinetic and Radiomics tabs. Numbers quoted below from those three tabs are synthetic seed values that show how the interface behaves. They are not study results. The TAC tab warns 'Raw PET data are not present locally. Cached analyses remain explorable.' The Connectivity tab shows a file-not-found error for its matrix inventory.

tree.general: Find out how far a dynamic imaging acquisition can be cut short or degraded before its quantitative conclusions become unreliable, and whether recovery methods restore them
tree.specific: Explore protocol robustness of dynamic brain PET endpoints (normalized AUC, model-free TAC features, kinetic covariance, dynamic radiomics) from cached KinetiQC benchmark outputs

features.name: Reconstruction comparison overlay with AUC error table
features.general: Pick an item, overlay the reference signal, the degraded signal and several reconstructions on one time axis, and judge each reconstruction by an integral error metric in a companion table rather than by how the curve looks
features.specific: In the 4-D PET / TAC Explorer, choose Subject, Condition and Harvard–Oxford ROI. The chart overlays Clean, Corrupted (40% masked; the uncorrected zero-fill baseline), Linear interpolation and Tiny timing-aware TCN TACs. The table lists duration-weighted AUC and absolute relative AUC error for each curve, and a frame-timing table follows. Values in this run come from synthetic seed data
steps: choose subject
choose condition
choose region
compare the overlaid curves
read the AUC-error table to rank the reconstructions
serves_tasks: Compare a clean curve against a corrupted one and two reconstructions, judged by area-under-curve error
Repeat the comparison for another region, subject and condition

features.name: Degradation-scenario picker with family-specific agreement metrics
features.general: Set several kinds of acquisition degradation, choose which one drives the view, choose an outcome family, and get two headline agreement metrics, a per-subject table and a curve of error against increasing severity
features.specific: In the Reliability Lab, four dropdowns (Scan duration, Temporal sampling, Count degradation, Motion) feed a 'Constraint to display' radio. The radio, not the last-touched dropdown, decides which dropdown selects the scenario. The Endpoint family dropdown (model_free, intervention, connectivity, radiomics) swaps the metric pair, for example median abs. relative error + CCC, or matrix edge Pearson + normalized Frobenius distance. A per-subject line chart plots the metric against severity order. Combinations outside the benchmark show 'This combination was not evaluated in the bounded matrix' (e.g. radiomics at 25% counts)
steps: set the degradation level in the matching dropdown
pick that constraint in the radio
choose the endpoint family
read the two metric tiles and the per-subject table, or the 'not evaluated in the bounded matrix' notice
read the severity curve to see where each subject degrades
serves_tasks: Pick a degradation scenario and an endpoint family, and read the per-subject agreement metrics and the degradation curve
Repeat for other kinds of degradation
